summary: Raphael Marozzi was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He earned a B.A. from the University of Washington around 1946–1949 and an M.A. from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa around 1949–1952.

Raphael von Koeber worked in philosophy and Japanology. He studied at the Moscow Conservatory, Heidelberg University, and the University of Jena, and took up a post at the University of Tokyo in 1893.

Rashmi Yadav works in Indology. She studied at Dr. B. R. Ambedkar University, Agra, earned a diploma from Chaudhary Charan Singh University, and joined its Faculty of Vedic Mathematics in 2021 before pursuing a Ph.D. at Mahatma Jyotiba Phule Rohilkhand University.

Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Fergusson College under Dr. Bhune and Ramchandra Dattatraya Ranade, as well as under Sukhlal Sanghvi and Muni Jinvijaya. He served as Professor at Gujarat Vidyapith (~1920–1930).

Rasmus Nyerup was an Indology scholar who earned an M.A. from the University of Copenhagen (~1779–1784). He held posts at the Royal Danish Library (1784–1803) and served as Chief Librarian at the University of Copenhagen (1796–1829).

Rasmus Rask was a linguist and scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Odense Katedralskole and the University of Copenhagen, where he later held posts including professor of literary history (1825) and chair of Oriental Languages (1831).

Ratna Basu is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. She completed doctoral studies at the University of Bonn by 1989 and is attested as a Professor (Special Invitee) at The Asiatic Society in 2026.

Ratna Handurukande is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Harold Walter Bailey. She served as a lecturer at the University of Peradeniya and as a lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Ceylon (attested 1970).
Ratna Vajra Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga, whom he succeeded in 2017.

Ravi M. Gupta is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Boise State University and the University of Oxford (D.Phil.), later teaching at William & Mary (~2008–2013) before becoming Charles Redd Chair of Religious Studies at Utah State University (~2013).

Ravi Prakash Arya is an Indologist who studied at Panjab University. His posts include Associate Professor in Haryana's Department of Higher Education (1993–2019), Chair Professor at Maharshi Dayanand University (2021–2025), and President of Vedic Science Virtual Vishva Vidyapeeth (2025).

Ravindra Singh Bisht is an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Lucknow, Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology, and Kumaun University, and eventually served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India until 2004.

Ravindra Suryakant Kale works in Indology and computational fields. He served as College Librarian at Narmada College of Management (2005–2014) and became Librarian at Shree Somnath Sanskrit University in 2014.

Ravinjay Kuckreja is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He earned a BA from the University of Chester (2014–2017), an MA from IE University (2017–2018), and a doctorate in Religious Studies from Universitas Hindu Negeri I Gusti Bagus Sugriwa (2020–2023).

Rawi Bhavilai was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned degrees from Chulalongkorn University, the University of Adelaide, and Australian National University, and served as a physics professor (1945–1986) and director (attested 2002) at Chulalongkorn University.
Ray Caldwell Smith was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at San Francisco Theological Seminary (~1897–1900) and held a post at the Landour Community Centre Language School.

Raymond West was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Galway and under Martin Haug. He served as Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1886–1892) and as a lecturer and Reader at the University of Cambridge (1895, 1901–1907).
Raymonde Linossier was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and archaeology. She studied under Sylvain Lévi (~1920–1930) and served as an unsalaried attachée at the Guimet Museum in 1925.

Reb Anderson is a Buddhist studies practitioner and teacher. He studied under Shunryu Suzuki and Richard Baker, whom he succeeded, and served as abbot of the San Francisco Zen Center from around 1986 to 1995.
Rebecca Hufen is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, she is a lector for Tibetan Studies and a doctoral student under Dorji Wangchuk at the University of Hamburg.
